dedupe_keys.name: real time ics scada system cyber kit testbed with industrial hacking scenarios

description: This Mendeley Data deposit gives network traffic from a portable industrial control system testbed built to produce labelled data for intrusion detection research. The kit has a Siemens SIMATIC S7-1200 PLC for process simulation, a SIMATIC basic HMI panel, a Scalance XB213 Ethernet switch with a mirror port that copies the operational technology traffic, analogue and digital input and output modules that imitate field devices, a passive deep-packet-inspection sensor, and an attacker machine running Kali Linux penetration tools. Four CSV files record stable normal operation and three attack scenarios: a man-in-the-middle attack between PLC and HMI, a Telnet attack on the PLC and a web-access attack on the PLC. Coverage is a single laboratory set-up, not tied to any country or plant. The dataset (version 1, 25 June 2021, author Sinil Mubarak) is free under CC BY 4.0 and totals about 14 MB. Caveats: the traffic comes from a small laboratory kit, not a real plant, only a few attack types are covered, and the process itself is simulated by input and output modules. For simulation it supports the cyber side of industrial infrastructure studies, such as training anomaly detectors or parameterising how a control-network intrusion interrupts a plant process in interdependency models. Related catalogue records include the NIST smart manufacturing systems test bed and the Tennessee Eastman process anomaly detection data.
